summary: Filesystem sandbox escape when renaming symlinks with trailing slashes
description:
## Impact

Wasmtime's filesystem implementation provided in the `wasmtime-wasi` crate contained a bug which allowed guests to escape their filesystem sandbox and read/write external directories. Guests provided write-access to any directory within their sandbox could move any directory on the filesystem the host process could access into their sandbox, and then read and write its contents. This bug is a full filesystem sandbox escape for guests.

This bug is closely related to [GHSA-vqjp-4c8c-hfgg](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/security/advisories/GHSA-vqjp-4c8c-hfgg). When renaming a file or directory, `wasmtime-wasi` strips a trailing slash from the source path to resolve its parent directory, but then re-appends the slash to the final path component before passing it to the `renameat` syscall. A guest could create a relative symlink pointing outside of its sandbox, for example `symlink("../outside", "up")`, and then rename `"up/"` to a path within its sandbox. The host kernel would then follow the trailing-slash symlink and move the directory outside of the sandbox into the sandbox. The fix for GHSA-vqjp-4c8c-hfgg only changed how paths are opened, not how they are renamed, so this affects all published versions of Wasmtime at the time of this advisory's publication.

This bug does not affect users on Linux or Windows, where `renameat` does not follow a symlink with a trailing slash. Users on macOS or FreeBSD, however, are affected by this issue. Only symlinks to directories can be used to escape the sandbox in this manner.

## Patches

Wasmtime 36.0.18, 48.0.6, and 49.0.3 are being released with this advisory which patches this issue.

## Workarounds

There is no known workaround for this issue. Users are recommended to upgrade to a patch release of Wasmtime that contains a fixed version of `wasmtime-wasi`.

## References

* [GHSA-vqjp-4c8c-hfgg](https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/security/advisories/GHSA-vqjp-4c8c-hfgg)
* bytecodealliance/wasmtime#14663 (the related `remove_dir` case)
